title: Plan the skill
body: Decompose the baseline defects before writing code: two-column interleaving, headers/footers leaking into body text, figure-internal vector labels, lost table/equation structure. Build a deterministic parser that never retypes text.

tool_args.cmd: pdftohtml -xml on a two-column paper; note that fontspec is document-global

title: shell
tool_output: <text> runs carry coordinates and font ids; <fontspec> appears only where a font is first used

title: Body font from a document-level font table
body: Per-page parsing drops the size of fonts first used on an earlier page, which mislabels body text as 10 pt and destroys every heading

title: Detect the gutter from geometry
body: Blank-column coverage fails when a spanning title crosses the gutter; cluster body-line left edges and require that >=50% of the left cluster closes before the right margin

title: shell
tool_output: cross-column lines 3.3% stream vs 0.1% skill; order inversions 7.6% vs 0.0%; marginalia 14 vs 0

title: Run-in heading captured as a section
body: Headings such as 'Decoder: The decoder is also composed of' were classified as level-2 titles

tool_args.cmd: Reject a heading whose text carries a colon followed by three or more words

title: shell
tool_output: sections 24 -> 23 on the single-column paper; heading tree 1 / 2 / 3.2.1 correct

title: Handle undecodable text layers
body: A CJK sample exposes 1512 'characters' that are all private-use codes; emitting them would be guessing characters

tool_args.cmd: Compare backend-readable characters against the raw text layer; below 20% report cannot_judge

title: shell
tool_output: CJK sample -> cannot_judge with reasons; encrypted -> reject; scanned -> cannot_judge

title: shell
tool_output: selfcheck PASS; 4 sections, 1 table, 1 equation, 3 references on the synthetic sample; wrote results/metrics.json

title: results/metrics.json
body: Measured metrics of the sample run

title: Cross-check
body: Every field in result.json is bound to a page and a bbox; selfcheck.py verifies the binding in both directions
